text: Git is a version control system that helps developers manage changes to their code. One of its most useful features is branching. A branch lets you work on new ideas without affecting the main code. For example, you can create a feature branch to build a new function safely. When your work is ready, you merge the branch back into the main project. In team settings, developers often open a pull request so others can review the changes before merging. This workflow keeps the project organized, reduces mistakes, and allows several people to work together at the same time.
